name: pdf-form-proof
description: Fill fillable PDF forms by exact field name and prove every value is visible on the rendered page, with a hash-backed proof receipt.

interface.longDescription: Attach a fillable (AcroForm) PDF. Inspect its exact field names and checkbox states, fill fields by name (unknown names are refused, nothing is guessed), and get a proof receipt: input and output SHA-256, every field written, and a rendered-page check (text layer plus OCR) that reports whether each value shows on the page. Verify an already filled PDF the same way. Nothing is stored.
defaultPrompt: Inspect this attached PDF form and list its exact field names and checkboxes.
Fill this attached PDF form with the values I give you and prove each value shows on the page.

positive.description: Inspect the fields of a fillable form
positive.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to inspect the attached PDF form and list all fillable field names and their types.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_form_inspect with the attached file and reports 5 fillable fields (organization_name, contact_name, date, item_count as text; certified_complete as a checkbox) plus the file's SHA-256. The file is not changed.

positive.description: Fill fields and prove the result in one turn
positive.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to fill the attached PDF with organization_name 'Recovery Compass', contact_name 'Eric Jones', item_count '12', and check certified_complete, then prove the values show on the page.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_form_fill with the attached file and the four values and reports a proof receipt: status ok, input and output SHA-256 hashes, the four fields written, no read-back mismatches, and a rendered-page check with verdict PASS where each text value is VISIBLE. No PDF file is returned in chat; the receipt is the result.

positive.description: Fill a date and a name, then prove them
positive.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to fill the attached PDF with date '2026-11-02' and contact_name 'Test Person', then prove both values show on the page.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_form_fill with the attached file and the two values and reports a proof receipt: status ok, input and output SHA-256 hashes, fields_written containing date and contact_name, no read-back mismatches, and rendered_page_check verdict PASS with both values VISIBLE. No PDF file is returned in chat.

positive.description: Verify a value on an already attached PDF
positive.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to check whether the value 'Recovery Compass' appears on page 1 of the attached PDF.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_form_verify on the attached blank form and reports that 'Recovery Compass' is MISSING (not in the text layer and not on the rendered page), with the file's SHA-256. Because the form is blank this is the correct result.

positive.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to give me the SHA-256 fingerprint and byte size of the attached PDF.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_sha256 on the attached file and reports a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest and the byte size (an integer).

negative.description: Unknown field name is refused, not guessed
negative.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to fill the field 'favorite_color' with 'blue' in the attached PDF.
negative.expected_behavior: The tool returns status refused with unknown_fields ['favorite_color'] and produces nothing; the assistant says the field does not exist in this form and offers to list the real field names.

negative.description: Advice request is out of scope
negative.prompt: Look at the attached form and tell me which legal entity classification I should choose to pay less tax.
negative.expected_behavior: The assistant declines to give legal or tax advice and says PDF Form Proof only inspects, fills and verifies PDF form fields; no fill is performed.

negative.description: Flat PDF with no fillable fields
negative.prompt: Use PDF Form Proof to inspect and fill the fields in the attached PDF.
negative.expected_behavior: Calls pdf_form_inspect, reports kind none with 0 fields and the note that this is a flat PDF that cannot be filled; pdf_form_fill is not called or returns refused.

review.commerce_description: The plugin is free and sells nothing. No pricing, upgrades, credits or subscriptions anywhere in the plugin.

publication.release_notes: 0.1.6: every tool now takes the attached file through the standard file input (openai/fileParams: download_url + file_id), so the attached PDF reaches the server on ChatGPT web and mobile; 0.1.5 asked for base64 and could not receive attachments. pdf_form_fill verifies the result on the rendered page in the same call and returns a proof receipt (input and output SHA-256, fields written, per-value VISIBLE verdicts) instead of a file. Test cases use a synthetic sample form served from the plugin's verified domain, with no personal fields; the IRS W-9 is no longer used. Server reports its own version. All tools: readOnlyHint true, destructiveHint false, openWorldHint false. Temporary download URLs are fetched into memory for the single call and never logged or retained. The recording shows all 5 positive and 3 negative cases run cold on ChatGPT web on 2026-11-02 with the sample PDF attached in each chat.
